articles.article5-p1: Mobile audits are usually limited to static code reviews or sporadic manual VoiceOver testing. VoiceOver A11Y Auditor brings the ecosystem's linear audit philosophy to iOS: it traverses the interface element by element inside the Xcode Simulator and literally documents what the screen reader announces.
articles.article5-h2-1: AXAudit Bridge: from simulator to report
articles.article5-p2: The core of the tool is AXAudit Bridge, a bridge that leverages Apple's accessibility audit services to enumerate the app's accessible hierarchy: labels, traits, values and on-screen frames. On that foundation, the auditor reproduces the VoiceOver rotor and swipe-gesture traversal, in the same order a user would experience it.
articles.article5-p3: The auditor is UI-technology agnostic: it evaluates UIKit views, SwiftUI components and web content embedded in WKWebView equally. For web views, it opens a Safari Remote Web Inspector (RWI) session to inspect the DOM, ARIA roles and even IndexedDB-persisted state, something unreachable from the native accessibility layer.
articles.article5-p4: The tool includes an adaptation layer for Apple Silicon chips (arm64) that normalizes differences between simulator architectures. Each run produces an interactive report with findings mapped to WCAG 2.2 criteria, traceable and repeatable, enabling integration into QA pipelines where only manual review previously fit.
articles.article5-p5: Saying a button "probably announces well" is not an audit. By capturing the real sequence of VoiceOver announcements and cross-referencing it with the accessibility tree and the RWI-inspected DOM, every finding is backed by reproducible evidence, the same yardstick applied by the ecosystem's NVDA and TalkBack auditors.
articles.article5-p6: The project is open source and available at github.com/ingelectronicadj/voiceover-a11y-auditor.
